judged_text: The appSlug values handed to the parent ('msteams' here, 'zoomvideo', 'google-calendar', 'hubspot', etc.) are bare magic strings with no compile-time tie to the appStoreMetadata keys and App-table slugs the webhook resolves them against, and 'msteams' matches no other identifier of this app anywhere in the diff (directory office365video, sibling references office365-calendar/office365_video). The parent keys its credentials by these strings and pushes them back to app-credential.ts, where prisma.app.findUnique({slug}) and appStoreMetadata[slug] must both resolve; if 'msteams' (or any of the nine hardcoded slugs) is not the exact seeded App slug / appStoreMetadata key, every MS Teams credential sync 404s in the webhook with no error surfaced anywhere on the Cal.com side, and Teams sync silently never works.

Nothing in the diff provides a compile-time/typed linkage between these literals and the canonical slugs used elsewhere (e.g. the `appStoreMetadata[...]` lookup and `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug } })` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`). However, the finding’s specific claim that this will definitively cause webhook 404s (because these literals are pushed “back to app-credential.ts”) is not directly verifiable from the diff: the webhook’s `reqBody.appSlug` is supplied by an external caller, and the diff doesn’t show that it is sourced from these literals.
